existing.description: WIPO's Fellowship Program places professionals in specialized disciplines at the World Intellectual Property Organization in Geneva, Switzerland, for 12 to 36 months. Fellows are classified into four categories: translation fellows in the PCT Translation and Terminology Fellowship Program, legal case manager fellows in the WIPO Domain Name Fellowship Program, visiting and research fellows in the Research and Visiting Fellowship Program, and other specialized fellows. Applicants must hold at least a first-level university degree, with additional requirements such as professional experience, an advanced degree or specific competencies depending on the category. Fellows receive a monthly stipend of CHF 3,000 to CHF 8,000 depending on academic background and relevant experience, comprehensive medical and professional accident insurance largely paid by WIPO, relocation assistance covering travel at the start and end of the fellowship, assistance with visa formalities, 10 official holidays plus 2.5 days of annual leave per full month, and access to WIPO Academy training with up to six study leave days a year. Positions are advertised through calls for expressions of interest on WIPO's career website and LinkedIn.
eligibility: At least a first-level university degree, for example a bachelor's degree
Depending on the fellowship category, a minimum level of professional experience
Depending on the fellowship category, an advanced degree such as a Master's or PhD
Depending on the fellowship category, specific competencies
No restriction on time since graduation
Former interns are welcome to apply if they meet the eligibility criteria
Young Experts Program participants are not allowed to apply for any position at WIPO within one year of finishing the programme
existing.eligibility_summary: At least a first-level university degree such as a bachelor's. Depending on the fellowship category there may be additional requirements, such as a minimum level of professional experience, an advanced degree such as a Master's or PhD, or specific competencies. There is no age limit and no limit on how long ago a candidate graduated. Former interns may apply if they meet the criteria, but Young Experts Program participants may not apply for any WIPO position within one year of completing the programme.

Comprehensive medical and professional accident insurance, largely paid by WIPO
Relocation assistance covering travel at the start and end of the fellowship
10 official holidays per year plus 2.5 days annual leave per full month
Up to six study leave days per year
WIPO-funded UN official languages training where required by job duties
coverage: Monthly stipend ranging from CHF 3,000 to CHF 8,000 depending on academic background and relevant experience

Comprehensive medical and professional accident insurance, with WIPO paying 100% of the medical premium for contracts under 12 months or 75% for contracts of 12 months or more, and 100% of the professional accident premium
Relocation assistance covering travel expenses at the start and end of the fellowship, plus assistance with visa formalities to Switzerland
10 official holidays per year plus 2.5 days of annual leave for each full month of the fellowship
Access to WIPO Academy internal training programmes, up to six study leave days per year, and WIPO bearing the cost of UN official languages training where required by the job duties
requirements: At least a first-level university degree
Any category-specific additional requirements stated in the individual call for expressions of interest
For former Young Experts Program participants, a waiting period of one year after finishing the programme before applying for any WIPO position
application_method: Monitor WIPO's career website for calls for expressions of interest, and WIPO's LinkedIn and other social media channels
Open the relevant call and submit an expression of interest through WIPO's Taleo career site
Meet the category-specific requirements set out in that call
Await WIPO's response; the page notes that reply times can vary because of the fast-paced nature of the programme
existing.selection_notes: Each fellowship is advertised individually as a call for expressions of interest and assessed against that category's requirements, which may include a minimum level of professional experience, an advanced degree or specific competencies. The page publishes no selection weighting.
existing.best_fit: Young professionals with at least a bachelor's degree and, depending on the track, a background in translation and terminology, law and internet or trademark dispute resolution, or economics and statistics, who want hands-on experience in intellectual property at an international organisation in Geneva.
existing.notes: The stipend is published as a range of CHF 3,000 to CHF 8,000 per month depending on academic background and experience relevant to the nature of the fellowship, so funding_amount is left null rather than picking one end of the range. This is a paid fellowship contract rather than a grant toward study costs, so no tuition component applies and full funding is not claimed. The page states the programme duration as 12 to 36 months while the benefits section describes contracts of up to 12 months renewable to a total of up to three years, which is consistent. A one-year waiting period applies to former Young Experts Program participants, which is a decision-critical rule that is easy to miss.
existing.duration: 12 to 36 months; contracts run up to 12 months with the possibility of renewal for a total of up to three years
existing.application_period: Continuous, per vacancy. Positions are announced through calls for expressions of interest on WIPO's Taleo career site and on LinkedIn, so there is no single application window.
existing.deadline_display: Fellowship positions may be advertised through calls for expressions of interest published on WIPO's career website, or via WIPO's LinkedIn or other social media channels. No fixed central deadline is published on the programme page.
existing.program_type: Professional fellowship programme of an international organisation, with four fellow categories

existing.eligibility_summary: Holders of a Swiss high-school maturity diploma or Swiss vocational maturity diploma undertaking the CMS. Outstanding results and engagement in school and extracurricular activities.
